section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes a study that explored the correlates of body appreciation (external shame, self-compassion, BMI) and the mediating role of self-compassion in the relationship between external shame and body appreciation in young male and female adults. Correlation analyses revealed a positive association between body appreciation and self-compassion, and a negative association with external shame for both sexes. For men, body appreciation did not significantly associate with BMI. Path analysis confirmed the suitability of the theoretical model for both men and women, suggesting self-compassion as an adaptive strategy against the impact of external shame on body appreciation. The section concludes by acknowledging methodological limitations, including the cross-sectional design and small sample size.
